svg.text: dmxbox 2: USB to two DMX512 outputs
PIC32MX270F256B as a USB network adapter, two isolated RS-485 outputs, ready for RDM · box number by DIP switch · every capacitor ceramic
USB-C and the supplies of the logic side
R1, R2: many breakouts have them already; then leave them out.
SW2 and SW3 share pins 4 and 5 with
the programmer: do not press them
Crystal and the capacitors at the microcontroller
C6 on VCAP is needed: the chip makes its own core voltage. Never join VCAP to 3.3 V.
The isolated 5 V for the DMX side: U3 bridges the gap
No other part reaches across the gap
Pins 3, 4 and 6 of U3 do not exist.
• Labels with the same name are one wire: every +5V is joined, every GND, every TX1 and so on.
• GND (logic side) and GND2 (DMX side) are never joined. Only U3 and the optocouplers reach across the gap.
• Every capacitor is ceramic. 100 nF ones sit right next to the pins they serve.
• The two DMX outputs share GND2 and the isolated 5 V. Each XLR: pin 3 Data +, pin 2 Data −, pin 1 common.
• U5 and U9 (receive), U6 and U10 (direction), R12 to R14 and R21 to R23 make the box ready for RDM:
• the firmware sends only, for now, and keeps U6 and U10 dark, so both drivers send.
• Not connected: pins 1 and 4 of every 6N137, positions 7 and 8 of SW1, pin 6 of J2.
Pins of the chips, seen from above
Pin 1 is next to the notch (or dot); the numbers go round anticlockwise.
U1: pins 1 to 14 down the left side, 15 to 28 up the right side.
6N137 and MAX485: 1 to 4 down the left, 5 to 8 up the right. PC817: 1, 2 left; 3, 4 right.
U2 (MCP1700), flat side towards you, legs down: 1 GND, 2 VIN, 3 VOUT.
U3 (RKK-0505S/H): pins 1 and 2 sit together at one end; pin 7 stands alone at the other.
SW1: switch k joins pin k and pin 17 − k.
